newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close down on Siam Cement, finance.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close down on Siam Cement, finance.

text.p: Thai stocks retreated another 1.23 percent on Wednesday on weak first quarter earnings of Siam Cement Plc and lingering jitters over the finance sector outlook, brokers said.

"Investors weren't happy with weak earnings of Siam Cement. They also didn't have confidence in the finance sector after the collapse of the Finance One -Thai Danu Bank merger plan," said Thanawat Patchimkul of Seamico Securities.
The composite SET index closed 7.01 points lower at 562.83 on thin 2.2 billion baht turnover.
Siam Cement, Thailand's largest cement producer, fell eight baht to 528.
The company said its consolidated first quarter net profit fell to 1.9 billion baht from 2.7 billion a year ago.
Market confidence in the finance sector looked shaky ahead of scheduled resumption of trade in troubled Finance One shares on Friday after a three-month suspension.
Brokers were concerned that Finance One's renewed trade may pull down the whole market, brokers said.
Brokers said investors preferred to stay on the sidelines as they waited for Thursday's release of key monthly economic indicators by the central bank on Thursday.
The SET-50 index fell 0.59 point to 40.69.
Most key sectors retreated. Banks lost 2.10 percent and the finance sector fell 2.97 percent.
Bangkok Bank topped the active list declining three baht to 146, Advanced Info lost four to 172, and Dhana Siam fell two to 20.25.
